                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> scatter.</ns0:note> cast them away as a menstruous cloth <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Thou shalt so deeply abhor Idolatry, that thou shalt cast away, with indignation, all the Monuments and Instruments thereof.</ns0:note>; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23. Then shall he give the rain of thy seed <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Or rather, as others render it, <ns0:hi>to</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>for thy seed,</ns0:hi> when thou hast newly sown thy Seed, which was called <ns0:hi>the for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer rain;</ns0:hi> or such as thy Seed requires, which may include both the former, and the latter Rain. Their Sins, the cause of all God's judgments which had befallen them, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing removed by their sincere Repentance, and God's gra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cious Pardon, God showreth down all his Blessings upon them.</ns0:note> that thou shalt sow the ground withal, and bread of the increase of the earth <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Which shall be the Fruit of thy own Land and Labour: which is a great Mercy and Comfort.</ns0:note>, and it shall be fat and plenteous <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Thy Bread shall be excellent for quality, which is called <ns0:hi>fat, Deut.</ns0:hi> 32. 14. and abundant for quantity.</ns0:note>: in that day shall thy cattel feed in large pastures.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:593" />24. The oxen likewise and the young asses that ear the ground shall eat <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> savoury.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> leave<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned.</ns0:note> clean <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Or, as Learned Mr. <ns0:hi>Gataker</ns0:hi> renders it <ns0:hi>Threshed,</ns0:hi> which agrees well with the following Clause, Corn being first Threshed, and then winnowed. The Sence is, There should be such plenty of Corn, that their very Beasts, instead of Straw, should eat Corn; and that not in the Ear, or with the Straw, but the pure Grain.</ns0:note> pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vender, which hath been winnowed with the sho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vel and with the fan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25. And there shall be upon every high moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain, and upon every <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> lifted up.</ns0:note> high hill <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Which are commonly dry and barren, and destitute of Rivers.</ns0:note>, rivers, and streams of waters, in the day of the great slaugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">When God shall destroy the Enemies of His People, He will shower down his Blessings upon his Church.</ns0:note>, when the towers <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Either properly, the Towers of <ns0:hi>Babylon;</ns0:hi> for which She was famous, or Metaphorically, the high and mighty Potentates, which fought against God's, people as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 2. 15.</ns0:note> fall.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26. Moreover, the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">For constancy and brightness: Which, as also the fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing Clause, is to be understood Metaphorically, of the most glorious and comfortable Condition of God's Church, for surpassing what it was in former Ages. And so this, as well as other passages in this Chapter, concerns the times of the Gospel.</ns0:note>, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">As if the Light of seven days were combined together into one: Its Light shall then be tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scendently more bright and glorious, than it hath hither<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to been. Which magnificent Expressions seem to be too high for the deliverance of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> either from <ns0:hi>Sennache<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rib,</ns0:hi> or out of <ns0:hi>Babylon:</ns0:hi> And do much better agree to the times of the Gospel, in which the Light is far more clear, and the grace of God much more abundant, than ever it was in former times. And this Exposition seems the more probable, because it is the manner of the Prophets; and especially of this, who is rightly called the <ns0:hi>Evangelical</ns0:hi> Prophet, to take all occasions to speak of the days of <ns0:hi>Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siah,</ns0:hi> and of the blessed Priviledges of that time and state of the Church, among which, they constantly reckon <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> whether you take it for Knowledge or for Comfort, to be one.</ns0:note>, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">When God shall effectually Cure the Wounds and Breaches of his People, first making up the Breach between Him and them, then making <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> to be one, who now are sadly divided; and making <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentile</ns0:hi> to be one Fold under one Shepherd, even the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> which the Prophets foretell, that it shall be in the times of the Gospel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27. Behold <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Here begins the last part of the Chapter, wherein he gives them an earnest of those greater Mercies pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised for times to come, by assuring them of the approach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Destruction of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Forces.</ns0:note>, the name of the LORD <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Lord him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self: For as <ns0:hi>the names</ns0:hi> of Men are oft put for the Men themselves, as <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 26. 53. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 1. 15. <ns0:hi>Revel.</ns0:hi> 3. 4. and 11. 13. So <ns0:hi>the name of God</ns0:hi> is frequently put for God, as <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 4. 26. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 28. 58. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 20. 1, 7. &c.</ns0:note> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth from far <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">From a ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry remote place; even from Heaven, whence God sent His Angel to destroy them, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 37. 36. Possibly this Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pression may respect the judgment of the <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> who looked upon God as one afar of, not onely in his Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sence, which they thought to be confined to Heaven, but in his care of, and affections to the <ns0:hi>Iews;</ns0:hi> and therefore, no more expected any opposition from Him, than from them who live in the ends of the Earth.</ns0:note>, burning with his anger, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> and the grievousness of flam<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> and the burden <ns0:hi>thereof</ns0:hi> is <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> heaviness.</ns0:note> heavy <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He will inflict heavy Judgments upon them.</ns0:note>: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">He hath pronounced a severe Sentence against them, and will give Command for the Execution of it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28. And his breath <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Either 1. <ns0:hi>The breath of his Nostrils,</ns0:hi> as it is called, <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>b.</ns0:hi> 4. 9. or <ns0:hi>The blast of the breath of his Nostrils,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 18. 15. in both which places it is mentioned, as a sign and effect of God's Anger, and the cause of the Destructi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of those, against whom it is directed. And the Expres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion seems to be borrowed from hence, that Men discover their Anger by a strong and vehement breathing through their Nostrils. Or 2. <ns0:hi>The breath of his Lips</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mouth,</ns0:hi> to which the destruction of God's Enemies is elsewhere ascri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bed, as <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 15. 30. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11. 4. which may be the same thing with <ns0:hi>his Lips</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Tongue</ns0:hi> in the foregoing Verse, or may design a strong blast coming out of his Mouth: for God is frequently said to destroy wicked Men, by <ns0:hi>blowing</ns0:hi> upon them, as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40. 7, 24. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 21. 31. and 22. 21.</ns0:note> as an overflowing stream <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Coming from Him as vehemently as a mighty Torrent of Waters.</ns0:note>, shall reach to the midst of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 8. 8<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> the neck <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Shall bring him into a most dangerous con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition, as a Man, who is in deep Waters which reach to his Neck, is in danger of being drowned; and afterwards, as is related in the following Verses, will utterly De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroy him. And this was fulfilled in <ns0:hi>Sennacherih,</ns0:hi> who was highly endangered, when he lost so great a part of his Army, and shortly after Slain by his own Sons. Although these words may be added as a description of <ns0:hi>the over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flowing stream</ns0:hi> now mentioned, and may be thus ren<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dred, which <ns0:hi>Reacheth even to the midst of the Neck;</ns0:hi> for the relative Particle is frequently understood in Scripture.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. 9. 9.</ns0:note> to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ift <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To shake and scatter, as it were with a Sieve: or to try and vex, as this Metaphor signifies, <ns0:hi>Amos.</ns0:hi> 9. 9. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 22. 31.</ns0:note> the nations <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Army, which was made up of the People of several Nations.</ns0:note> with the sieve of vanity <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Not with an ordinary Sieve, which casteth away the Chaff onely, and keepeth the Corn; but with a Sieve, which should shake them so long and so ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hemently, as to cast away all together, and to make a full End of them.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:hi>there shall be</ns0:hi> a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 37. 20.</ns0:note> bridle in the jaws of the people <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">God will restrai<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> and over-rule them by His secret and powerful Providence.</ns0:note>, causing them to err <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Whereas other Bridles guide the bridled Creatures into the right way, this shall turn them out of the way, by giving them up to their own Mistakes, and foolish Counsels, and wicked Courses, which shall bring them to sore and certain Ruine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29. Ye shall have a song <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">You shall have occasion of great Joy, and songs of Praise for your stupendious Deliverance from that formi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dable Enemy.</ns0:note>, as in the night, <ns0:hi>when</ns0:hi> a holy solemnity is kept <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">He mentions the Night, either because the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Feasts begun at the Evening, and were Cele<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brated with great Joy in part of the Night-season, as well as on the following Day; or because He hath a particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lar respect to the solemnity of the Passover, in which they spent some considerable part of the Night in Feast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and Rejoycing, and singing of Psalmes and Songs be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the Lord.</ns0:note>, and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a Pipe <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Like the joy of one that is going up to the solemn Feasts with musick, and the voice of Joy and Praise, as they used to do, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 42. 4. to cheer up them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves in the way, which to many of them was long, and would otherwise have been tedious.</ns0:note> to come into the mountain of the LORD, to the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>rock.</ns0:hi> Deut. 32. 4.</ns0:note> mighty one of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30. And the LORD shall cause <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> the glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry of his voice.</ns0:note> his glori<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous voice <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">His Thunder, which is called God's <ns0:hi>Voice,</ns0:hi> and said to be <ns0:hi>full of Majesty, Psal.</ns0:hi> 29. 4. But then Thunder is Metaphorically taken for some terrible Judgment, as it is in many places of Scripture.</ns0:note> to be heard, and shall shew the light<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing down of his arm <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Upon the <ns0:hi>Assyrian,</ns0:hi> whom He will smite with a deadly blow in the face of the World. The Phrase is taken from the gesture of a Man, who is about to smite another; who first lifts up his hand, and then lets it fall with great force upon him, whom he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signs to strike.</ns0:note>, with the indignation of <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> anger <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">With great wrath; which is signified by the heaping of so many words of the same signification together.</ns0:note>, and with the flame of a devou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring <ns0:hi>fire, with</ns0:hi> scattering, and tempest, and hail<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stones.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31. For through the voice of the LORD <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">That Voice mentioned in the last Verse.</ns0:note> shall the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> be beaten down, <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> smote with a rod <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Which was the Rod wherewith God smote His and other people, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 10. 5, 6. He who used to smite others, shall now be smitten himself. Or, as the words may be, and by others are rendred, <ns0:hi>He</ns0:hi> (the Lord last mentioned) <ns0:hi>shall smite</ns0:hi> him <ns0:hi>with a rod,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>rod.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">32. And <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> every passing of the rod founded.</ns0:note> in every place where the grounded staff <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Heb<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                        <ns0:hi>the founded rod,</ns0:hi> the Judgment of God, which is frequently called a <ns0:hi>Rod</ns0:hi> in Scripture, and may be here cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>a founded Rod,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>the Rod of Foundation;</ns0:hi> either because it was firmly established, and certainly to come by God's immutable Purpose and Appointment: or because the Rod should not slightly touch him, and pass over him, but strike deep, and be fixed; and as it were grounded or founded in his Flesh; and made to rest upon him, as it follows in the next Clause.</ns0:note> shall pass, which the LORD shall <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> cause to rest upon him.</ns0:note> Iay upon him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Upon the <ns0:hi>Assyrian,</ns0:hi> mentioned in the fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />going Verse.</ns0:note>, it shall be with tabrets and harps <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Sence is, Either 1. their Destruction shall be Celebrated, by God's People, with joy and musick, and songs of Praise, Or 2. the Victory shall be got, not by warlike Instruments and Atchievements, but as it were by Tabrets and Harps. Wherein He may possibly allude to the Victory which <ns0:hi>Iehoshaphat</ns0:hi> got against <ns0:hi>Moab</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Am<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon,</ns0:hi> not by fighting, but onely by singing, and praising God with the Voice, and with musical Instruments, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 20. 19, 21, 27, 28. God being pleased to Fight for them, by his own immediate Power; which also was the case here, which made the People of God sing a Triumph be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the Fight, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 37. 22.</ns0:note>: and in battles of shaking <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>with battles or fightings of shaking,</ns0:hi> to wit, of shaking of the hand, of which kind of Shaking this <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word is constantly used, such as are performed by the meer shaking of the hand; namely, by God's shaking His Hand against them, as He threatens to do against others, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11. 15. and 19. 16. in which last place this very word is used; and in the former, the Verb from whence it comes. For that this Shaking is an Act of God, seems more than probable, and from the fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing words, <ns0:hi>Will be,</ns0:hi> i. e. God, as all understand it, <ns0:hi>fight against it.</ns0:hi> And so the Sence of the place may be this, God will Fight against them, and destroy them by His own Hands,</ns0:note> will he <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To wit, the Lord, who declareth himself to be the Enemy of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian,</ns0:hi> both in the foregoing and fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing Verses.</ns0:note> fight <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> against them</ns0:note> with it <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">With the Army of the <ns0:hi>Assyrians:</ns0:hi> Or, according to the other <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> reading, <ns0:hi>with them,</ns0:hi> with the <ns0:hi>Assyrians.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>. <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>shall cause to rest;</ns0:hi> which is contrary to the manner of God's dealing with His People, upon whom He will <ns0:hi>Not suffer the rod of the wicked to rest, Psal.</ns0:hi> 125. 3.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:593" />33. For <ns0:hi>Tophet</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This was a place near <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> in which the Idola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trous <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> used cruelly to Offer up their Children to <ns0:hi>Moloch,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 28. 3. and 33. 6. See also <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 7. 31. and 19. 6. And it may be put Synecdochically, for any place of Torment or Misery: And particularly it is put for Hell, as well in the Writings of the ancient <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Doctors, as in holy Scripture, as <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 18. 8, 9. and 23. 15. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9. 43. 44. And so this place may be understood: Either 1. literally of <ns0:hi>Tophet</ns0:hi> in the Valley of <ns0:hi>Hinnom,</ns0:hi> in which the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Host was, either slain by the Angel, as <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> reports, or buried, or burnt. For although the <ns0:hi>Assyrians</ns0:hi> did not make any great attempt upon <ns0:hi>Ierusalem, Isa.</ns0:hi> 37. 36. yet <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh</ns0:hi> came very near it with a great Army, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 36. 2. Or 2. figuratively of Hell.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> ordained <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or, was <ns0:hi>orde<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>prepared.</ns0:hi> And it might be said, in some sort, to be Prepared by <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> for this end, by the care which he took to Purge this and other places, abused to Idolatry, which made them more fit to receive so great a Favour and Deliverance from God. But for Hell, that doubtless was Ordained or Prepared by God, for the punishment of impenitent Sinners.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from yesterday.</ns0:note> of old <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>From yesterday:</ns0:hi> Which phrase is sometimes used of a time but lately past, as <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 8. 9. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15. 20. and sometimes of any time past, without limitation.</ns0:note>: yea, for the king <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">For the King of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> Either 1. for the Kings, the <ns0:hi>Singular</ns0:hi> Number being put for the <ns0:hi>Plural,</ns0:hi> where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by he may understand the Princes, or chief Commanders of the Host, by comparing <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 10. 8. <ns0:hi>Are not my Princes altogether Kings.</ns0:hi> Or 2. for <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh,</ns0:hi> the General of this Army, who, according to the style of Scripture, might ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry well be called King. Or 3. for <ns0:hi>Sennacherib;</ns0:hi> for whom this place might be said to be Ordained or Prepared: partly because it was Ordained for the Destruction of his Host; nothing being more ordinary, both in sacred and prophane Writers, than to intitle the King, or General of the Army, to all the Victories procured, or Losses and Slaughters sustained by his Army: And partly because the sudden Destruction of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Army, supposed to be in this place, was the occasion of the Conspiracy of that King's Sons, and so of the King's Death. But if this <ns0:hi>To<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet</ns0:hi> design Hell, this is Emphatically den<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
